description: Run capa (capability rule matches) and FLOSS (recovered strings) over one PE or ELF file, if the programs are installed, and keep what each said: the whole JSON of each, its stderr, its argv and what its --version printed, and the rules that matched (matches.tsv: name, namespace, ATT&CK ids, count; no feature and no string). An engine that is not installed, fails, is stopped at its time limit or writes JSON of a shape this recipe does not read is a named status of that engine and the recipe is partial or failed, never complete. A FLOSS string kind whose own analysis flag (enable_*) is false was not run, and makes the floss result partial. The receipt, the index and matches.tsv pass the same sanitiser and backstop as the pack's tools (withholding by shape only: a secret of another shape is printed). An engine's JSON over 32 MiB is kept whole and not read, and that engine is partial. Not run automatically: it is requested for a sample whose capabilities or obfuscated strings are in question.
covers: What capa and FLOSS each wrote about a PE or ELF file, as the program said it (coverage.json: per-engine status, argv, version output, exit code, bytes; limits_hit, warnings, errors). A rule match is a hypothesis about what the code could do and a recovered string is derived; neither is behaviour, reachability or intent. It does not run the sample, does not run an engine that is not installed, and a status other than complete names what is missing. capa.json and floss.json can hold credentials: coverage.json, index.tsv and matches.tsv copy none.
